messages:
pagerbot: P1 alert — Unusual auth traffic + debug logs found in staging S3 bucket. Possible API key fragments detected. Alert: https://internal-alerts.example/8201112223 :rotating_light:

morgan: acked, joining. tagging @ashley for sec lead. can someone take triage ownership?

ashley: I got it. onsec -> I'll lead. quick ask: any customer-facing buckets involved or just staging?

raj: quick dump — looks like a recent deploy flipped DEBUG=1 on a staging lambda. Logs shipped to s3://staging-debug-logs/ starting 2026-03-19T22:10Z. indexer job also triggered that bucket sync yesterday.

evan: cs: if this hits any customer tokens tell me now so we can prepare comms.

ashley: immediate actions: 1) block public access to bucket, 2) snapshot bucket for forensics, 3) rotate any exposed keys, 4) run a quick scan for key patterns. i'll coordinate.

raj: evidence — run to check ACL right now:
```
aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket staging-debug-logs
```
output snippet: 
```
Grants:
  - Grantee: URI "http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AllUsers"
    Permission: READ
```
This shows public-read. :eyes:

morgan: omg. oncall running playbook now. @deploy-bot can you disable public access and suspend downstream indexer?

deploy-bot: Executing runbooks -> disable-public-access.sh; suspending indexer sync job.

deploy-bot: Done. set-bucket-public-access-block: true, suspended indexer job id indexer-sync-20260319. timestamp 2026-03-20T01:02:30Z.

ashley: good. preserve bucket contents for forensics but mark read-only snapshot. @jules legal needs preservation notice.

jules: Confirmed. do not delete or alter originals. create immutable snapshot and record chain-of-custody. I need a copy of the list of exposed keys (redacted) and who had access.

raj: quick grep script I'm running to find probable key exposures in objects:
```
aws s3api list-objects --bucket staging-debug-logs --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text | xargs -n1 -I {} sh -c 'aws s3 cp s3://staging-debug-logs/{} - | strings | egrep "(sk_live|sk_test|api_key=|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16})" && echo "--- {} ---"'
```
Will post hits.

raj: first pass results: found 3 object keys with short API fragments and one full-looking service key id: AKIAEXAMPLE12345678 (redacted). Listing object paths: logs/2026-03-19/inst-42/debug.log, logs/2026-03-19/worker-7/out.txt, tmp/sync/trace-001.txt

ashley: rotate immediately: service principal used by staging-lambda, and any long-lived deployer keys. run rotation playbook: zap-keys.sh -> revoke and reissue. Also add quick WAF deny for any traffic matching header patterns from suspicious IPs.

morgan: @ashley i'm handing incident ownership to you for the next shift. i'll stay on standby until keys rotated. set incident channel topic to "ashley lead — staging s3 exposure"

evan: cs draft for customer-facing note (for review): "We detected debug logs from a staging environment that contained snippets of API keys. There is no evidence of production customer data access. We have secured the staging assets, rotated affected keys, and are investigating. We'll notify customers if we find any customer data." feedback?

ashley: good draft. add estimated timeline: will confirm rotation completion within 2 hours and follow up with a summary.

raj: rotation progress: revoked role credentials for staging-lambda (role: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/staging-lambda), rotated deployer service account keys (key id AKIAREPLACEME), restarted lambda with DEBUG=0, redeployed without log shipping.

deploy-bot: actions complete: public access removed, indexer suspended, role credentials revoked, snapshot created: s3://forensics/staging-debug-snapshot-8201112223.tar.gz

ashley: next steps: 1) run broad grep across backups and CI artifacts, 2) scan CI logs for tokens, 3) rotate any user-facing tokens if found, 4) update deploy checklist to block DEBUG in lambda configs. assigning tasks: raj -> repo/backup sweep, morgan -> CI pipeline scan, evan -> prepare comms template, jules -> legal hold docs.

raj: running backup sweep now. preliminary: found one paste in an old artifact pipeline that included an API token pattern — expired token, but rotating anyway.

morgan: CI scan done — flagged two builds that had masked logs but stack traces stored resolved tokens; marking as rotated.

ashley: we should also run a traffic correlation to see if any external IPs used extracted tokens. raj/infra run a short-lived honeypot to see if anything active.

raj: correlation query run against auth logs for the past 48h: `index=auth earliest=-48h | search "AKIAEXAMPLE" OR "sk_live"` — no successful production usages found. only staging footprints.

evan: CS: preparing a short customer bulletin, legal reviewed. will hold send until we confirm no customer creds in the exposed files.

jules: also start a JIRA with evidence tag and add legal owners + retention policy. ticket INFSEC-820111.

ashley: final note for this thread: containment complete (public ACL removed, keys rotated, indexer suspended, snapshots saved). impact: staging-only; no production customer data seen so far. continuing forensic sweep and will escalate if anything changes. :shield:

morgan: leaving oncall. ashley you're owner. ping if you need escalation. :thumbsup:

ashley: thanks all, closing the live page for now but keeping the channel open for updates. will post postmortem draft in 48h.
